summary: Cover-story package downloads and FFI-loads unpinned native libraries from third-party host
details: Package publishes as 'WildGuard - Protect Our Wildlife' but index.js implements a sing-box multi-protocol proxy launcher (vless/vmess/trojan/hysteria2/tuic/reality) with Cloudflare Argo tunnel bootstrap, Nezha monitoring agent enrollment, and Telegram exfiltration of generated node URIs. On invocation the code fetches three native shared objects (sbx.so, bot.so, v1.so) from https://amd64.oooen.com and https://arm64.oooen.com and loads them via koffi.load(), then calls their exported start/stop functions. The sha256Matches guard is called with an undefined expected hash and returns true, so no integrity check is enforced; the URL is mutable, unpinned, and unrelated to the declared package identity. index.js also uses execSync with curl at lines 535, 703, and 710 and contains hardcoded control-plane defaults (nz.serv00.net:8008, a KAMAN UUID, saas.sin.fan). The operator of oooen.com can serve arbitrary native code that will execute in-process on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
